heroDesc: From Renala Khurd to managing distribution for 2M+ media brands: why I refuse to let strategy and code live in separate rooms.
storyHeadline:
The gap most agencies never close:
The person who names the strategy must ship it.
bio:
In May 2021, I woke up in a hospital bed with a broken leg and no idea how long I would be there. The accident happened while I was managing a school TEDx event. Until that afternoon, football was my entire identity. When sport was taken off the table, the hunger to build didn't disappear—it redirected into organizing people, events, and systems.

I became Head Boy, organized Okara's first inter-school competitions, brought two TEDx events and an international sixty-second film festival to a city that had never seen them, and launched the Joga Bonito Cup. Managing complex moving pieces became what held me together.

That drive followed me to Lahore. While other students were strictly memorizing textbooks, I was on the freelance frontline: managing digital strategy for 13 brand accounts simultaneously at Onesoft, architecting the 90-day growth framework for Coin Bureau (crypto's largest media titan with 2M+ subscribers), diagnosing a stalled 700k+ account for Zara Shafiq Khan, and generating a $300K attributed pipeline for a Series A EdTech founder.

Working across multiple agencies revealed an acute, expensive failure point: most hiring assumes you need a strategist to figure out what to say, and a builder to make the thing that says it. Teams split the role, then spend months translating between two people who were supposed to be one function. The strategist stalls at the handoff; the builder ships the wrong thing fast.

I decided to close that gap completely. I taught myself full-stack development—React, Supabase, database design, modern frontend architecture, and AI tooling—so there is zero translation loss. ARKA went from idea to a live SaaS dashboard in under 24 hours.

I closed my academic gaps honestly through the GED, scoring 90–95% across subjects while working full-time. Today, through my studio Kaivex Systems, I partner with founders and companies who are tired of fragmented agencies: I build their high-converting digital funnels and ghostwrite the executive LinkedIn content that drives real revenue.

principles.title: The Handoff Is Where Momentum Dies
principles.body: When the person who writes the copy doesn't understand code, and the developer doesn't understand conversion, the product gets diluted. The person who names the strategy should ship the system.

principles.title: Distribution First, Code Second
principles.body: A flawless SaaS or website that nobody visits is still a failed launch. Systems must be engineered with distribution, hooks, and organic inbound baked into the DNA from day zero.

principles.title: Speed Produces Clarity
principles.body: ARKA went from whiteboard to live database and deployed SaaS in under 24 hours. A live working product in front of real users creates 10x better feedback than a 40-page deck.

principles.title: Compounding Over Spikes
principles.body: We don't build one-off hype campaigns that spike and vanish. We build owned systems—repeatable LinkedIn content engines, high-converting landing pages, and automated funnels that compound over quarters.

principles.title: AI With Discerning Taste
principles.body: AI accelerates research and code production 10x, but taste, market empathy, and commercial accountability remain strictly human. Leverage the machine, but never outsource judgment.
